problem: Temporal QA benchmarks under-represent questions with implicit time constraints (e.g. "during the Cold War"), use hand-crafted templates with low diversity, and draw answers from a single source type (KB or text).
method: TIQ (Temporal Implicit Questions): automatic question construction with systematic control of topical diversity, timeframe, and head vs. tail entities; questions formulated from diverse snippets and paraphrased by an LLM; supporting snippets drawn from KB, text and infoboxes.
key_assumptions: Implicit temporal constraints can be generated systematically and answered from multi-source snippets
Wikipedia-style knowledge sources are representative of temporal QA
main_contribution: A 10,000-question benchmark for temporal QA with implicit time constraints, with ground-truth answers and supporting evidence snippets.
datasets: TIQ benchmark (10,000 questions with ground-truth answers and supporting snippets)
limitations: QA benchmark rather than a retrieval-version benchmark: snippets are not successive revisions of the same provision with dense semantic overlap
No version/validity timestamps at passage granularity are described
Baselines and metrics are not available from the abstract, so benchmark comparability cannot be judged

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: TIQ tests whether a model can interpret and use implicit time constraints across KB/text snippets; the proposed benchmark would test version selection among overlapping amendments with per-passage version timestamps.
relation_to_idea.basis: Relevant mainly as an evaluation resource: it is a temporal QA benchmark with supporting evidence, but it does not model overlapping successive document revisions. Basis is the abstract only.
